the superlubrification in the graphene/h-BN system originates from the collective sliding of Moiré super-structures.

we show that graphene/h-BN junctions are a robust superlubric material.
superlubricity is a general property of layered materials, and the superlubricity can be further enhanced by the heterojunctions between two layered materials.

The main takeaway from our work is that

superlubricity is not only a consequence of the incommensurability of two-dimensional materials interfaces, but also depends on the nature of the contact, which in turn is dictated by the relative orientation of the two materials.
the superlubrigicity in heterostructures is robust and can be achieved even in misaligned contacts.

the sliding friction of layered material interfaces is not only determined by their intrinsic atomic-scale properties, such as the interlayer interaction strength, but also by the relative alignment and the resulting Moiré patterns.
